name: KPI Store
description: The graph the KPI Store's local Neo4j load builds from the release's Turtle with n10s. The Turtle is the master copy; this document is written from it and never edited by hand.

Resource.description: Every node n10s loads from the release. Its uri is unique (the constraint n10s_unique_uri).

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

con_Rule.description: A rule for an agent that answers from the graph: what it may answer without reading a table or inventing a formula, or what it must refuse.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

core_CanonicalFact.description: One relationship fact between two processes, as a node that names its subject, predicate and object and carries the workbook rows that support it. The direct triple stays; the node is its evidence record.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

core_evidenceRow.description: A relationship-workbook row (REL ID) that supports the fact. A fact carries every distinct row that supports it. Not core:sourceRow, whose domain is the scoped sequence.

core_ScopedSequence.description: A scoped sequence states that, for each instance of a named scope unit, a stated part of an earlier process happens before a stated part of a later process. Neither process needs to complete.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

core_linksToAncestor.description: True when one endpoint is an ancestor of the other in the process taxonomy. Allowed only where a source-author answer states that sequence explicitly.

core_sequenceCondition.description: The condition under which the sequence holds, in the words of the definition sentence. Absent when the sequence holds for every instance of the scope unit.

core_sourceRow.description: The relationship-workbook row (REL-nnnnn) the node was reviewed from.

dp_DataProduct.description: A named, governed set of data that a business area publishes for others to use, defined by what it covers. A definition, never the data: the platforms that hold the data product hold its records.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

dp_DataProductLine.description: A group of related data products in one segment of the portfolio, such as Energy Trading & Risk Management.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

dp_PlatformColumn.description: A value column of a platform table, recorded only where its lineage is recorded: the price columns.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

dp_columnName.description: The column's name, as the table spells it.

dp_PlatformDataProduct.description: A platform table or view that is published as a governed data product, as part of a data product of the portfolio, and classified as foundational or derived. A replica table is a platform table but not a platform data product: it copies a system's own records.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

dp_classificationReason.description: Why the data product has its kind, in a sentence.

dp_PlatformTable.description: A table or view on a data platform, named by its full name (catalog, schema and name), in one layer of the platform: replica, silver, gold or metric view. A definition of the table, never its rows.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

dp_fullName.description: The table's or view's full name on its platform: catalog, schema and name.

dp_sandbox.description: True when the table is in a sandbox catalog, not production; its name changes when the production name is recorded.

dp_PortfolioSegment.description: One of the portfolio's top-level groups of data product lines: Commercial, Midstream or Corporate. Each is anchored in a part of the process map.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

kpi_MeasureDefinition.description: What a measure is, before anyone computes it: its meaning, kind, grain, basis and the processes it informs. A definition, never a value: the systems that compute the measure hold its values.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

kpi_basis.description: How the measure is formed, in words: its numerator, its denominator and its unit. A description, not a formula the ontology computes.

kpi_classificationReason.description: Why the measure has its kind, in one or two sentences.

kpi_classificationTest.description: The number of the test, from 1 to 5, in the decision of 2026-10-18's rule that assigned the measure's kind.

kpi_comparedAgainst.description: The references the measure is asked against: plans, forecasts, plan versions or history. For a plan-variance diagnostic the comparison is part of the measure. For any other kind it is a way of asking for the same measure, not a second measure.

kpi_grain.description: The time and dimension the measure is stated at, for example daily by refinery.

kpi_kpiCandidate.description: True when industry practice and public information make the measure a strong KPI candidate. It becomes a KPI only by a recorded decision that names its target and owner.

kpi_publicCounterpart.description: The measure MPC publishes that is closest to this one, by its number in mpc-performance-measures-evidence.md, or none.

pop_excludes.description: What the measure leaves out, in business words, as its source states it.

pop_includes.description: What the measure counts, in business words, as its source states it.

pop_populationEvidence.description: Where the population statements come from.

lane_OfficeLane.description: One of the four office lanes of the trading organization.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

lm_LogicalModel.description: A named logical data model exported from a data modelling tool, such as ER Studio Data Architect: a set of entities, their attributes, keys and relationships, designed one level above the tables a data platform builds. Each model is one individual of this class, and the entities of its export belong to it.

mkt_Benchmark.description: A published price that a series is built from: a crude marker, a refined-product benchmark at a named market, or a compliance cost such as the RVO.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

mkt_priceMasterId.description: The identifier MPC's price data (MPR Price Master) gives the series or input price. An identifier, not a price.

mkt_reportedAs.description: How the pricing view reports the price: basis (a differential to the futures contract), cash, differential, settlement or assessment.

mkt_BenchmarkSeries.description: One published series of a market measure, identified by what it is built from: its region, its crude and product legs and their ratio, and what it leaves out. Two series of the same measure are different series when any of these differ.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

mkt_excludesRINCost.description: True when the series does not reflect the market cost of RINs, as MPC's 10-K crack spreads do not (MPC Economics' Inc-RVO treatment). False when the series deducts the RVO cost (MPC Economics' Ex-RVO treatment, which MPC's price data labels ex-RIN). A series with RIN costs and one without are different series.

mkt_priceMasterId.description: The identifier MPC's price data (MPR Price Master) gives the series or input price. An identifier, not a price.

mkt_reportedAs.description: How the pricing view reports the price: basis (a differential to the futures contract), cash, differential, settlement or assessment.

mkt_Leg.description: One part of a series' recipe: a benchmark and the number of barrels of it.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

mkt_barrels.description: The number of barrels of the benchmark in the recipe, as in the 3 and 2 and 1 of a 3-2-1 crack spread. A ratio, not a price.

mkt_MarketPrice.description: A named market price that a pricing measure of the kpi module presents, as the decision owner's pricing views report it: a product price at a market, a crude differential, a futures settlement, or a renewables or NGL price. A definition, never a price.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

mkt_priceMasterId.description: The identifier MPC's price data (MPR Price Master) gives the series or input price. An identifier, not a price.

mkt_reportedAs.description: How the pricing view reports the price: basis (a differential to the futures contract), cash, differential, settlement or assessment.

mkt_SeriesEnumeration.description: Where the complete list of a measure's series is: a view and the columns that identify, name and group each series, with the rows' filter. The module names only examples; the view lists them all.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

mkt_groupColumn.description: The view's column that groups the series.

mkt_idColumn.description: The view's column whose distinct values are the series.

mkt_nameColumn.description: The view's column that names each series.

mkt_rowFilter.description: Which of the view's rows belong to the measure, in words, as the agent's filters state it.

mkt_sourceView.description: The full name of the view that lists the series, catalog, schema and view.

orgm_ControlRelationship.description: One legal entity's control of another, with the ownership share, the date it held and its source. A node of its own because it carries a share and a date. Separate from org:subOrganizationOf, which means a unit inside one organization.

orgm_ownershipShare.description: The fraction of the controlled entity the controlling entity owns, from 0 to 1, as the source states it.

A node of its own, because a single property cannot bind a role, a process and a level together. Design-time responsibility, not a record of who did the work.

party_Agreement.description: The commercial frame that party roles work under. It sets terms, pricing, volume, product scope, brand, territory, exclusivity and assignment rights. Its types overlap: one agreement can have several.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

party_Brand.description: A trademark a product is marketed under. The network carries owned, licensed and competitor brands. A brand is owned by or licensed to a party for a period, through a Brand License agreement.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

party_ContactPoint.description: A telephone number, an email address or a fax number through which a party can be reached. It records its usage type and the period it is valid for.

It holds the account status, payment and credit terms, the company-code assignment, settlement details and the period it is valid for. The customer class is assigned at this level.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

party_PartyTransactionAssociation.description: The link of a party role, or of an account, to one transaction, with the role it played there. A transaction can be an order, a ticket or bill of lading, an invoice, a payment or a case, or a trade or transfer captured in a deal. It records the transaction reference, the role, the account and the period it is valid for.

graph.description: The version IRI of the release the element was loaded from (the module tag the load writes).

party_pidxProductFamily.description: The one-letter family of PIDX's downstream product codes that the product's PIDX codes belong to. A plain identifier: PIDX publishes no IRIs, and a PIDX code names one company's traded grade, so the product is not mapped to PIDX codes.

party_Site.description: A physical operating location with its own lifecycle, whoever owns it: a station, a bulk plant, a cardlock, a terminal, an airport location or a pipeline delivery point. It records its operating model, amenities, image compliance and the terminals that supply it. A party owns or operates it for a period, through a party role held at the site.
